title: Lufthansa Adds Second Daily Munich–Delhi Flight in Biggest Expansion Since 2020
excerpt: Summer 2027 brings more Frankfurt flights to Hyderabad and Chennai, extra Munich–Bengaluru frequencies and a retained SWISS Zurich–Bengaluru link — all bookable since October 20.
body:
• Lufthansa will add a second seasonal daily Munich–Delhi flight from March 28, 2027, on an Airbus A350-900, in the Lufthansa Group's biggest network expansion since 2020.
  • Frankfurt gets more frequencies to Hyderabad and Chennai, Munich adds frequencies to Bengaluru, and SWISS keeps its five-times-weekly Zurich–Bengaluru service.
  • The Summer 2027 schedule — 10 new destinations group-wide, including Columbus (May 5) and Phoenix (August 3) in the US — has been bookable since October 20, 2026.
  • For diaspora travellers, the added Delhi, Hyderabad, Chennai and Bengaluru capacity means more one-stop options from US gateways via Frankfurt, Munich and Zurich — and more award and sale inventory on the busiest India routes.

Lufthansa is doubling down on India for Summer 2027. The German carrier will operate a second seasonal daily flight between Munich and Delhi from March 28, 2027, using an Airbus A350-900, and will raise frequencies from Frankfurt to Hyderabad and Chennai and from Munich to Bengaluru. The India build-up sits inside the Lufthansa Group's largest network expansion since the pandemic — 10 new destinations across its airlines, on sale since October 20, 2026.

"A total of ten new destinations and even more new connections represent not only the largest route expansion across our six Lufthansa Group hubs in a long time, but above all a promise to our guests: even more choice, even better connectivity, and even shorter journeys."

— Stefan Kreuzpaintner, Senior Vice President Commercial Customer Offer, Lufthansa Group

The India Changes, Route by Route

Delhi gets the headline move: a second daily Munich service for the summer season, flown by the A350-900, Lufthansa's long-haul workhorse on India routes. Hyderabad and Chennai gain additional frequencies from Frankfurt, the group's largest hub, while Bengaluru — already one of the fastest-growing India stations — gets more Munich frequencies. Switzerland's SWISS, also a group carrier, will keep its recently launched Zurich–Bengaluru service running through Summer 2027 at five flights a week, according to the schedule reported by Travel Trade Journal.

The group has not published the exact new weekly frequencies for the Hyderabad, Chennai and Bengaluru increases — those load into booking systems as the schedule firms up — but the direction is unambiguous: every one of Lufthansa's four Indian gateways grows or holds in Summer 2027.

Why India, Why Now

India is among the fastest-growing long-haul markets in the world, and European carriers are racing Gulf rivals for the traffic between India and North America — much of it diaspora travellers connecting over a European hub. Lufthansa's answer is capacity at all three of its relevant hubs: Frankfurt, Munich and Zurich. The same schedule adds US capacity that feeds those India flights, including more Chicago frequencies from Munich and two new American nonstops — Frankfurt–Columbus from May 5, 2027 (three times weekly, Boeing 787-9) and Munich–Phoenix from August 3, 2027 (three times weekly, A350-900).

What Travellers Can Do With It

The Summer 2027 programme is already bookable — the group opened sales on October 20, 2026 — so diaspora families planning summer 2027 trips to Delhi, Hyderabad, Chennai or Bengaluru can price the new options now, including the second Munich–Delhi departure, which doubles the daily connection banks out of southern Germany. Travellers comparing routings can check the full schedule announcement via Travel Trade Journal's route-by-route breakdown and the original Hotelier Buzz report. More seats on the four busiest India corridors usually means better odds on sale fares and mileage seats — worth an early look before the summer peak prices in.
